region.name: Founder Router Reckoning
region.summary: Private reflections from a founder/CTO navigating the Series B, the Sep 26 SEV1 incident, and board communication, while confronting their role as a decision bottleneck through delegation plans, VP Eng handoffs, and commitments to a sustainable personal pace.

brief.text:
This region holds the private journal and therapy-adjacent reflections of the company's founder/CTO during a high-pressure stretch: closing a Series B, absorbing the Sep 26 SEV1 incident (an ACH double-debit), preparing for a board meeting, and recruiting a VP Eng. The central theme is the founder's recognition, named in therapy, that they are 'the router': nearly every decision passes through them. Being needed feels like safety, yet the Sep 26 incident happened anyway. The founder traces the habit to a misread lesson from April and a personal need to be needed. The response is a delegation rule: decisions that are reversible, within an owner's area, do not involve money, and do not touch the Pillar posture go to the owner. Five decision areas were assigned to named owners, with SOC 2 evidence, the experiment freeze, and incident postmortem lessons among the areas discussed. An Oct 8 update splits responsibilities into what stays with the founder until the VP Eng starts (incident commander and Pillar remediation are relevant here) and what transfers on the VP Eng's first day. It also leaves open the question of whom the VP Eng hire is meant to relieve, and it admits that delegation was announced but the founder is still delaying the Ama decision.

The board-prep reflection compares what the deck wants to say (the term sheet, ACH reliability, MAU growth, the investing beta) with what it avoids (the SEV1 double-debit, risk to investing GA, SOC 2 gaps, and the CTO as a single point of failure). It argues for leading with the bad news so that it lands as an answer and not as a question from the board. Open tracked items in the region include a written remediation plan owed to Pillar (todo, severity 19), two GA blockers still open (risk, severity 19), investing GA at risk for the Oct 20 date, a capacity model built on average load instead of peak load, and key-person risk concentrated in the CTO (each a risk at severity 4). The engineering response to the incident is ADR-024, an architecture rebuild started with Marcus, together with a process change. The founder also worries that Marcus is copying the founder's own router habits.

The personal side covers burnout and the commitments made to address it. The founder reports 5 hours of sleep, no gym since August, and no visit to their parents since July. Agreed actions include booking a flight to see their parents, a weekly date night, 30 minutes of non-work reading each night, a laptop-free Sunday (elsewhere a laptop-free Saturday), writing down what it means to stop being the router, handing off three recurring decisions before the VP Eng starts, telling one colleague they are tired, and a follow-up session with the therapist. One daily plan lists the gym, an ADR-024 walkthrough, a support follow-up with Renee, and a check-in with Aleks. One entry deliberately stops the self-blame over the incident. The founder frames the work as having no natural end point, so a sustainable rhythm has to be self-imposed, and treats the Series B year as hard but the kind of hard they want. Typical questions this region can answer: which decisions the founder delegated and to whom, what stays with the founder before the VP Eng arrives, how the board should hear about the SEV1 and the GA risk, what is owed to Pillar, and what the founder committed to for their own pace and health.

items.title: Decision: Adopt weekly sustainability habits

items.title: Open Question: Can the 27-engineer team build the 60-engineer org?
items.summary: Unclear whether the team that built the 27-person org can scale to 60; some will struggle and some thrive, and which is which is unknown.

items.title: Open Question: Who is the VP Eng hire relieving?
items.summary: Unclear whether the VP Eng is hired to take load off the founder or off Marcus; it must be both, which may change the ideal candidate.
